paragraphs: The Landrace is the long white pig with ears that fall forward over its eyes, and those ears are the identification: no other common breed carries them that way. The body is correspondingly long, bred for bacon rather than for bulk, which gives the animal a quite different profile from the compact breeds.

The mesh is light at 16,029 polygons and 16,205 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 15 texture maps at a mix of sizes up to 4096x4096 carrying the skin, the sparse bristles and the dirt.

This page carries walking and standing poses at the same $79 and a rigged build at $99. Aimed at farming and livestock visualisation, food industry and agriculture material, education content, advertising and games. Built to StemCell specification, on sale since 2019.

A moulded fibreglass frame lets a bicycle take shapes a tube frame cannot: continuous surfaces flowing from the head tube back to the rear dropouts, with no visible joints and no triangulation. The result looks more like a scooter body than a bicycle, which is exactly the retro-futurist effect the design is after.

The mesh is 196,572 polygons and 209,176 vertices, built entirely from quads. The UVs overlap, sensible on a symmetrical moulded body, and all-quad geometry is the right choice for surfaces this smooth because it subdivides cleanly.

At $79 and built to StemCell specification, it suits concept and product design presentation, retro-futurist and lifestyle advertising, urban visualisation, film and television, and games. On sale since 2026.

A pocket watch shown open is a different object from a closed one: the hinged lid stands out at an angle, the dial is visible with its hands and subsidiary seconds, and the case profile reads as a mechanism rather than as a disc. That open position is what makes the piece look owned and used.

The mesh runs 138,358 polygons and 140,615 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the density in the case edge, the hinge, the bow and the dial furniture where a close product camera lands.

A gold version sits on this page at the same $79. Both suit jewellery and watch e-commerce, luxury advertising, period film and television, still life and character props, and games. On sale since 2022.

The wartime Red Army uniform is austere by design: a pullover tunic with a stand collar and no front opening below the chest, wide breeches gathered into boots, a canvas belt and the distinctive steel helmet. That pullover cut is the detail most reconstructions get wrong, and it is what dates the uniform precisely.
The mesh is efficient at 23,943 polygons and 24,408 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which suits a costume usually needed on several figures at once in a period scene.

At $79 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits historical film and television, museum and commemorative material, documentary work, education, reenactment reference and games. Real-world scale is kept, so it fits a standard figure. On sale since 2025.

A surgical robot is a cart with four arms and a surgeon sitting some distance away at a console. The arms are the striking part: long jointed booms that converge over the patient, each carrying an instrument or the camera, arranged so they can work through incisions barely wider than a pencil.

The mesh runs 231,922 polygons and 240,471 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 30 texture maps at 4096x4096 carrying the moulded housings, the sterile drape fittings and the labelling.

A rigged build sits on this page at $99 for when the arms have to move. The static model at $79 covers surgical and medical visualisation, hospital and theatre interiors, medical device marketing, training material and games. On sale since 2018.

A tube launched loitering munition folds into a canister barely wider than the fuselage: the wings swing out on release, the tail surfaces deploy, and the pusher propeller starts. That folding arrangement is what lets one soldier carry a precision weapon in a backpack, and it defines the airframe's proportions.
The mesh is light at 23,130 polygons and 12,067 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which suits a weapon that appears in numbers rather than alone.

A second build sits on this page at the same $79. Both suit defence and modern warfare visualisation, news and documentary graphics, training and analysis material, and games. Real-world scale is kept, so it sits correctly relative to a launch tube. On sale since 2023.

A textile workroom is full of small specific objects: shears, rotary cutters, tailor's chalk, measuring tapes, bobbins, seam rippers and pin cushions. Individually they are trivial; together they are what makes a workshop scene look like a place where garments are actually made rather than a table with a sewing machine on it.
Supplying them as a collection keeps the scale and the finish consistent across the whole bench, which is the detail that betrays a scene assembled from separate sources.

At $79 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits fashion and textile industry visualisation, atelier and workshop interiors, craft and vocational education material, retail and editorial imagery, and games. On sale since 2026.

The trophy is a figure caught mid stride with the ball tucked and the free arm out in a stiff arm, mounted on a stepped base. That pose is the whole design and it is instantly recognisable to anyone who follows the college game, which means the arm angle and the lean have to be right or the object stops working.
The mesh is light at 11,911 polygons and 6,013 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the figure and the base moulding where the silhouette is read.

A black version sits on this page at the same $79. Both suit sports broadcast graphics, college and athletics presentation, award and ceremony visualisation, advertising and games. Built to StemCell specification, on sale since 2023.

Shown in flight, a loitering munition is a different asset from one on a launcher: wings extended, tail surfaces out, propeller turning and no launch hardware attached. That is the configuration a strike graphic or an analysis piece actually needs, and it is the one most models do not provide.
The mesh is deliberately light at 12,289 polygons and 12,920 vertices in quads and tris with mixed UV layout, which is right for a weapon shown in numbers or at distance.
At $69 and built to StemCell specification, it suits defence and modern warfare visualisation, news and documentary graphics, procurement and training presentation, and games. On sale since 2026.

Post never arrives as one item. A doormat, a sorting bench or a delivery scene needs a mix: padded envelopes, small boxes, letters of different sizes, a tube, something with tape over a corner. That variety is the whole point of a collection, because repeating one parcel across a pile immediately looks wrong.
Supplying them together also keeps the paper and card materials consistent, so the whole pile reads as coming from the same postal system rather than from three different renderers.

A second collection sits on this page at $89 for a wider selection. This set at $69 is aimed at logistics and e-commerce visualisation, delivery and courier marketing, interior and hallway scenes, film and television set dressing, and games. On sale since 2019.

A robotic radiosurgery system is an industrial arm carrying a compact linear accelerator, moving around a patient couch to deliver beams from many directions. That is the whole clinical argument: no fixed gantry, so the radiation can approach from angles a conventional machine cannot reach.

The mesh runs 75,480 polygons and 76,009 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, ships with 9 texture maps at 4096x4096, and arrives rigged so the arm can be posed or animated through a treatment path.

A build prepared for Cinema 4D sits on this page at the same $69. Both suit oncology and radiotherapy visualisation, medical device marketing, hospital interiors, patient education and training material, and games. On sale since 2019.

A head with a specific hairstyle and makeup is a styling reference rather than a generic bust. The bob has to fall with a real weight line and a blunt edge, and the makeup has to read as applied product rather than as painted skin - both of which are decisions a portrait model has to commit to rather than avoid.
The mesh runs 23,496 polygons and 32,775 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the vertex count running above the polygon count as hair geometry usually does.

At $69 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits beauty and cosmetics visualisation, hair and salon presentation, fashion and editorial imagery, character design reference, and games. On sale since 2025.

A land border crossing is a piece of infrastructure with a very specific choreography: a canopy over the lanes, booths between them, barriers that lift, signage overhead and a secondary inspection area to one side. That layout is what makes a checkpoint read as a border rather than as a toll plaza.
The mesh runs 144,530 polygons and 147,674 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the canopy structure, the booths and the barrier assemblies.

At $59 and built to StemCell specification, it suits border control and customs visualisation, security industry and government presentation, news and documentary graphics, road and transport scenes, and games. On sale since 2025.

A newt is defined by its skin and its tail. The skin is granular rather than smooth, quite unlike a frog's, and the tail is flattened side to side for swimming rather than round like a lizard's. Those two features are what place the animal correctly as an amphibian rather than a small reptile.

The mesh is minimal at 6,254 polygons and 3,143 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which suits a small animal whose realism comes from skin texture and wetness rather than from geometric density.

A standing pose sits on this page at the same $59. Both suit wildlife documentary and education, biology and ecology material, conservation content, children's education and games. Built to StemCell specification, on sale since 2024.
